skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, artifacts, posters, or applications (examples include websites, landing pages, dashboards, React components, HTML/CSS layouts, or when styling/beautifying any web UI). Generates creative, polished code and UI design that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
skill.summary: Guides creation of polished, distinctive frontend interfaces with strong visual direction.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: The three static findings are false positives caused by design-language phrases in SKILL.md. The skill contains only frontend design guidance and no evidence of system reconnaissance, data exfiltration, code execution, or prompt injection. No remediation is required.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 7 describes the skill's frontend design purpose and asks for working interface code. It does not request host inspection, environment discovery, or system reconnaissance.
Line 30 gives typography guidance for visual design choices. It contains no instruction to enumerate system fonts, inspect files, or gather host details.
Line 34 recommends visual background treatments such as textures and shadows. This is aesthetic guidance, not a command to probe the system or collect data.

content.value_statement: Generic web interfaces feel interchangeable and may miss the user's brand or product context. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to design polished, functional frontends with a clear visual direction.
actual_capabilities: Helps choose a bold aesthetic direction before implementation.
Guides HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, and similar frontend work.
Encourages distinctive typography, color systems, motion, spatial composition, and visual details.
Promotes production-grade, functional interfaces instead of static mockups.
Directs Claude to avoid common AI design cliches and repeated palettes.
limitations: Does not include runnable helper scripts or generated assets.
Does not test accessibility, responsiveness, or performance by itself.
Relies on user-provided project context and available framework dependencies.
May need human review for brand, legal, and accessibility compliance.

use_cases.title: Design a Landing Page
use_cases.description: Create a memorable launch page with clear hierarchy, strong visual identity, and working frontend structure.

use_cases.title: Improve a Product Dashboard
use_cases.description: Turn a plain operational screen into a polished interface with better density, rhythm, and visual priorities.

use_cases.title: Build an Interactive Prototype
use_cases.description: Generate a frontend prototype with refined styling, motion, and responsive layout choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new standalone interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a polished landing page for [product]. Use [framework]. Choose a distinctive visual direction and explain the main design choices.

prompt_templates.title: Style an Existing Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for improving a component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this [component] for [audience]. Keep the behavior unchanged. Improve typography, color, spacing, and motion.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Dashboard Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a practical application screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production-ready dashboard for [workflow]. Include responsive layout, clear hierarchy, useful states, and a coherent theme.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Frontend System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a multi-screen product interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a multi-screen [app type] interface. Define the aesthetic direction, component patterns, interaction states, and implementation plan before coding.

output_examples.input: Build a product launch page for an AI writing tool.
output_examples.output: A responsive page concept with distinctive type, clear sections, interactive calls to action, and implementation notes.

output_examples.input: Restyle a plain settings page for a B2B app.
output: A refined settings interface with grouped controls and clear scanning paths.
A restrained visual system that supports repeated daily use.
Interaction states for toggles, destructive actions, and saved changes.

output_examples.input: Create a SaaS analytics dashboard for retention data.
output_examples.output: A dense, readable dashboard with charts, filters, empty states, responsive behavior, and a consistent design language.

best_practices: Provide product goals, audience, preferred stack, and existing design constraints.
Ask for responsive states, accessibility considerations, and real interaction behavior.
Review generated designs against brand needs before production use.
anti_patterns: Requesting a generic modern design without context or audience.
Accepting decorative effects that reduce readability or performance.
Using the skill as a substitute for accessibility testing or user research.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create polished frontend pages, components, dashboards, prototypes, and interface styling.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate working frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for functional frontend code when the user requests an implementation.

faq.question: Does it include scripts or dependencies?
faq.answer: No. The package contains written design guidance and a license file only.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production design work?
faq.answer: It can support production work, but teams should still review accessibility, performance, and brand fit.

faq.question: What context should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide the product purpose, audience, stack, brand constraints, and target screens.
